images.text:
Hear ye! Hear ye! Friends, Romans, Countrymen! Lend me your ears! My name is Paula Timbers and I am so happy to be here giving my first Toastmasters address. I would like to give a special thanks to my friend Howard Taylor who signed my petition to join the club.
Today I would like to talk to you about my recent trip to China. I went with three other brave employees from my office. I am convinced that going on this trip was a great decision. In preparation for the trip, I read several histories of China and also learned about Chinese language and philosophy. In my opinion, the best language course out there is the classic series called Getting By in Chinese. I combed through several travel guidebooks for pictures of some major landmarks to be able to identify them when I got there.

When I arrived in Beijing, I found that the legacy of Chairman Mao is prominent everywhere. I walked around for nearly an hour and a half, soaking up the ambiance of the busy streets, buildings and traffic. As a Canadian traffic engineer, I was fascinated to see horses, pedicabs and cars parked on sidewalks, and every kind of transport you could imagine on the side streets. You have to be adaptable to get around in China.

Then there is Tiananmen Square — a public square larger than any other in the world. Ninety football fields would fit inside it. When I was there, it was filled with soccer players, kite-flyers and of course all kinds of people who were just out for a walk. I stopped for a while and chatted with a couple who told me they were students. I suspect they wanted to practice their English. They said they studied art and calligraphy. I was interested, so they kindly invited me to look at their work. What an experience!

You can learn how to pronounce new words more easily if you know some simple rules about suffixes and word stress.

You can learn how to stress a word by paying attention to the rules for certain suffixes. A suffix is the ending of a word that adds meaning to that word. Knowing the meaning of suffixes can increase your vocabulary and help you to express yourself in different ways, using different words.
Let's look at the following suffixes and their pronunciation rules for word stress.
